chunks: From him, from Bunan ibn Muhammad, from Sa'd ibn al-Sindi, from Ali ibn Abdillah ibn Imran, from al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:

Al-Rida (peace be upon him) said: "When you are in the Fajr prayer, and you have finished [the initial two rak'ahs] and see the dawn, add one rak'ah to the two rak'ahs you prayed previously, and make it odd [i.e., three total]."

key_terms.وَتْرًا: Odd (referring to an odd number of rak'ahs, typically 3 in this context)

ai.seo_question: How should the Fajr prayer be performed if one finishes the initial rak'ahs before dawn fully breaks?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) outlines a specific juristic opinion regarding the Fajr prayer, suggesting that if dawn is observed after completing the initial two rak'ahs, one should add a third rak'ah to render the prayer odd (witr). This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding the number of rak'ahs in Fajr, contrasting with the more common four-rak'ah practice, and emphasizes the significance of the dawn light as the precise marker for prayer timing. It reflects the scholarly tradition of deriving practical legal nuances directly from the Imams' instructions on ritual purity and timing.
